Corpulence is a noun that refers to the condition of being excessively overweight — having a body that carries a notably large and heavy amount of flesh or fat. It does not merely mean being a little chubby or slightly overweight. It points to a significant, visible, and substantial degree of heaviness in a person's body.

Think of it this way: if you walk into a room and a person's large, heavy physical size is immediately noticeable — something you'd describe as remarkable or considerable — that is what corpulence captures.

Corpulence describes a state or condition, not an action. It is the fact of being that way. So when you use this word, you are naming a quality that exists in someone — the quality of having an excessively heavy, fleshy body.

It is closely tied to its adjective form: corpulent, which means "excessively fat or overweight." Corpulence is simply the noun version — the name of that condition.

"His corpulence made it difficult for him to climb the stairs."

Here, corpulence refers to the condition (his excessive body weight) that was making something hard for him.

This is important. The word does not apply to someone who is slightly plump or a few pounds heavier than average. Corpulence suggests a very noticeable, substantial level of excess weight — the kind that is obvious to any observer and that may affect the way a person moves, breathes, or carries out everyday activities.
The Tone and Register of the Word

This is a formal, literary word. You will rarely hear it in casual, everyday conversation. People are far more likely to say "he's very overweight" in normal speech. Corpulence belongs to:

  • Written literature (novels, essays, journalism)
  • Formal descriptions (historical writing, biographies)
  • Medical or clinical contexts (older texts especially)

Because of this formal quality, the word carries a somewhat detached, observational tone. It describes a physical reality without the same emotional sting as cruder slang, but it is also not entirely neutral — in many contexts, it can carry an implied judgment or criticism, depending on how it is used. A skilled writer might use it clinically; another might use it to subtly mock or criticize.

Here are several examples showing how corpulence is naturally used:

  1. "The king's corpulence was well known across the kingdom — he could barely mount his horse."
  2. "Years of indulgence had led to a state of corpulence that alarmed his doctor."
  3. "Despite his corpulence, he moved with surprising speed and grace."
  4. "The portrait showed a man of great corpulence, his waistcoat straining against his girth."
  5. "She wrote in her diary about the corpulence she had developed after years of little exercise."

Notice that in each sentence, corpulence is used to describe a serious, visible degree of overweight — not a mild heaviness.
How It Differs from Similar Words

Several words exist in this space, and knowing the differences will sharpen your understanding:

  • Obesity — This is the modern clinical/medical term for the same condition, defined by measurable criteria like Body Mass Index (BMI). Corpulence is older, more literary, and less clinical.
  • Fatness — Straightforward and blunt. Corpulence is more formal and elevated in register.
  • Portliness — This word is softer and almost affectionate. A "portly" person is stout and rounded, but the word carries little negativity. Corpulence is heavier (pun intended) in its implication — it suggests a greater degree of excess weight.
  • Rotundity — Focuses more on the roundness of shape. Corpulence focuses on the weight and fleshiness.
  • Plumpness — This is mild and often carries a warm, even positive tone (a baby's plumpness is cute). Corpulence is never mild or warm — it always implies excess.

How much?A significant and visible degree — not mild
Where used?Formal writing, literature, older medical texts

Corpulence is the formal, literary word for the condition of being excessively and noticeably overweight — carrying far more bodily flesh and weight than is typical or healthy.

If you can remember that image — a person whose large, heavy body is immediately, unmistakably noticeable — you have captured exactly what corpulence means.
